name: pytest:api gate is a false green — it collects only 35 of the api tests
description:
## Finding (QA gate, shift 2026-11-18)

The API suite used as the merge gate is a **false green**: it does not collect the folder where the code is red.

Measured with the QA tools (same cwd `api`, same interpreter, only the path argument differs):

| Invocation | Tests collected |
| --- | --- |
| `qa_run_tests(suite="pytest:api")` | **35 passed** (allow) |
| `qa_run_tests(suite="pytest:api", paths=["tests/ai/smol"])` | **151** (150 passed, 1 failed) |
| `qa_run_tests(suite="pytest:api", paths=["tests/ai/smol/test_model_transport.py"])` | **24** (23 passed, 1 failed) |
| `qa_run_tests(suite="pytest")` (repo root) | **1386** (1373 passed, 5 failed, 1 skipped) |

Consequences:
1. A change can pass `pytest:api` while `api/tests/ai/smol/test_model_transport.py` (and the rest of `tests/ai/**`) is never executed. That is exactly the situation today.
2. The root suite and the api suite do not collect the same tree (35 vs 1386), so a verdict taken from one cannot be compared with the other — this is why shift-1 numbers (105 passed / 1 failed) were not reproducible.
3. `npm:wiki` is **unavailable** (`npm not found in PATH`) → the client tests cannot be gated at all (HIGH environment finding, still open).

Additional environment finding:
- `read_folder` and `project_locate` both **time out after 120 s** on this repository, so code discovery in the QA gate is impossible and every localisation has to be done by re-running the runner.

## What to do
1. Inspect the `pytest:api` suite definition (`qa_policy` → `suites`) and make its command collect the whole `api/tests` tree, or declare the intentionally excluded paths **with a reason** in `ignore_paths`.
2. Fix the collection pitfall at its root (e.g. a `testpaths`/`--ignore` in `api/pytest.ini`/`pyproject.toml` or the suite argv), then confirm the numbers line up: `pytest:api` should report the same test count as `pytest` restricted to `api/`.
3. Make `npm` available in the runner image (or formally disable the `npm:wiki` suite in `qa_policy` so it stops being reported as an unavailable suite).

## Acceptance criteria
- `qa_run_tests(suite="pytest:api")` collects ≥ 151 tests (i.e. includes `tests/ai/smol`) and its count is explained against the root suite's 1386.
- `qa_plan` no longer reports any suite as unavailable without a documented reason in `qa_policy`.
- A deliberate red test placed in `tests/ai/smol` makes the `pytest:api` gate fail (proof the gate really runs it).

Do **not** silence the suite or lower the policy; the gate must widen, not narrow.

messages.content:
## Finding (QA gate, shift 2026-11-18)

The API suite used as the merge gate is a **false green**: it does not collect the folder where the code is red.

Measured with the QA tools (same cwd `api`, same interpreter, only the path argument differs):

| Invocation | Tests collected |
| --- | --- |
| `qa_run_tests(suite="pytest:api")` | **35 passed** (allow) |
| `qa_run_tests(suite="pytest:api", paths=["tests/ai/smol"])` | **151** (150 passed, 1 failed) |
| `qa_run_tests(suite="pytest:api", paths=["tests/ai/smol/test_model_transport.py"])` | **24** (23 passed, 1 failed) |
| `qa_run_tests(suite="pytest")` (repo root) | **1386** (1373 passed, 5 failed, 1 skipped) |

Consequences:
1. A change can pass `pytest:api` while `api/tests/ai/smol/test_model_transport.py` (and the rest of `tests/ai/**`) is never executed. That is exactly the situation today.
2. The root suite and the api suite do not collect the same tree (35 vs 1386), so a verdict taken from one cannot be compared with the other — this is why shift-1 numbers (105 passed / 1 failed) were not reproducible.
3. `npm:wiki` is **unavailable** (`npm not found in PATH`) → the client tests cannot be gated at all (HIGH environment finding, still open).

Additional environment finding:
- `read_folder` and `project_locate` both **time out after 120 s** on this repository, so code discovery in the QA gate is impossible and every localisation has to be done by re-running the runner.

## What to do
1. Inspect the `pytest:api` suite definition (`qa_policy` → `suites`) and make its command collect the whole `api/tests` tree, or declare the intentionally excluded paths **with a reason** in `ignore_paths`.
2. Fix the collection pitfall at its root (e.g. a `testpaths`/`--ignore` in `api/pytest.ini`/`pyproject.toml` or the suite argv), then confirm the numbers line up: `pytest:api` should report the same test count as `pytest` restricted to `api/`.
3. Make `npm` available in the runner image (or formally disable the `npm:wiki` suite in `qa_policy` so it stops being reported as an unavailable suite).

## Acceptance criteria
- `qa_run_tests(suite="pytest:api")` collects ≥ 151 tests (i.e. includes `tests/ai/smol`) and its count is explained against the root suite's 1386.
- `qa_plan` no longer reports any suite as unavailable without a documented reason in `qa_policy`.
- A deliberate red test placed in `tests/ai/smol` makes the `pytest:api` gate fail (proof the gate really runs it).

Do **not** silence the suite or lower the policy; the gate must widen, not narrow.

QA evidence for this card — the false green has a second, worse half: **the gate cannot run the api tests at all**.

1. `qa_review_changes(scope="staged", suite="pytest:api")` → `run pytest:api: exited with code 5` (pytest *no tests collected*), while the *same* file run manually is green: `qa_run_tests(suite="pytest:api", paths=["tests/security/test_secrets_prompt.py"])` → **6 passed, 0 failed, 11.1s**.
2. Root cause hypothesis (high confidence): the gate builds the mapped-test argv from **repo-root-relative** paths (`api/tests/security/test_secrets_prompt.py`) but executes with `cwd=api` (suite `pytest:api`), so pytest receives a non-existent path → exit 5 → `tests.run-error` on every review that touches `api/`. Consequence: **any diff in `api/` can never be verified by the gate**, it always degrades to `require_approval` with a bogus run-error.
3. Collection numbers are the same family as the false green: `pytest:api` collects **35** tests from its default root; adding `paths=["tests/ai/smol"]` collects **150**+ in the same cwd; `tests/ai/smol/test_model_transport.py` alone = 24 (23 passed / 1 failed, 4/4 runs). So the default suite root is a subset of the tree, not the tree.

Acceptance criteria for the fix (owner `software_developer`):
- A review of a change under `api/` must pass the mapped test paths **relative to the suite cwd**, and `qa_review_changes(scope="staged", suite="pytest:api")` must stop emitting `tests.run-error` when the mapped file is green.
- The default `pytest:api` invocation must collect the same set as `python -m pytest -q` from `api/` (currently 35 vs 1000+); publish the collected count in the verdict so a silent subset is visible.
- Proof command: `qa_review_changes(scope="staged", suite="pytest:api")` → `tests_selected ≥ 1`, `passed: true` for the mapped file, no `tests.run-error`.

## QA evidence 2026-11-18 14:0x — root cause reproduced as an A/B, exit code corrected

**Corrected detail:** the failure exit code is **4 (usage error)**, not 5. Exit 5 = "no tests collected"; the gate's mapped-test invocation dies earlier, on argv it cannot resolve.

**A/B on the same suite, same file, only the path prefix differs**

| # | call | result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A | `qa_run_tests(suite="pytest:api", paths=["api/tests/security/test_secrets_prompt.py"])` | `exit code 4`, 0 passed / 0 failed, **4.4 s** → `tests.run-error` (medium) |
| B | `qa_run_tests(suite="pytest:api", paths=["tests/security/test_secrets_prompt.py"])` | **6 passed**, 0 failed, 20.3 s → decision `allow` |

Suite definition read back from `qa_plan`:
`pytest:api` → `cwd='api'`, `command=[<api>/.venv/bin/python, -m, pytest]`.

So the mapped-test argv the gate builds uses **repo-root paths** (`api/tests/...`) while the process starts with **cwd=`api`** → pytest cannot resolve the path → usage error → `tests.run-error` on *every* review that touches `api/`. Piece A returns in 4.4 s without running a single test, which is exactly the shape of a false green: `run_tests=True` but nothing executed.

**Acceptance criterion for closing this card:** `qa_review_changes(scope="staged")` on a change containing `api/` files returns `tests.run-error` = none, and the evidence line reports `passed ≥ 1` — i.e. the mapped paths are rewritten relative to the suite `cwd` (or the gate runs from the repo root). Re-verify with A above: it must stop returning exit code 4.

## QA follow-up 2026-11-18 14:07 — the mechanism is path resolution, not `cwd` alone (4 measured points)

| # | source | suite (declared cwd) | path passed | exit | tests |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `qa_run_tests` | `pytest:api` (`api`) | `tests/security/test_secrets_prompt.py` | **0** | **6 passed**, 20.3 s |
| 2 | `qa_run_tests` | `pytest:api` (`api`) | `api/tests/security/test_secrets_prompt.py` | **4** | 0, 4.4 s |
| 3 | `qa_run_tests` | `pytest` (`.`) | `api/tests/security/test_secrets_prompt.py` | **4** | 0, 0.9 s |
| 4 | `qa_review_changes(scope="staged")` | `pytest` (default) | *mapped test, emitted by the gate* | **5** | 0 |

Reading:
- The **only** form that executes a test is the path **relative to `api/`** (row 1). A repo-root path (`api/tests/...`) dies before collection with exit **4** in *both* suites (rows 2–3) — including the suite declared `cwd='.'`, so the declared `cwd` is not what sets the process working directory: this runtime resolves relative paths from `api/` (same reason `project_read_file` cannot see `wiki/...`).
- The gate's own run (row 4) fails with exit **5 = nothing collected**, a second symptom of the same misresolution, and it reports it as medium `tests.run-error` while `passed: 0` — i.e. `run_tests=True` executed **nothing** on a 23-file change and still returned `require_approval` instead of a run failure.

**Fix direction (for `software_developer`):** emit mapped-test paths relative to the directory the process actually runs in (`api/`), and treat `passed == 0` with `tests_selected > 0` as a hard failure so an empty run can never be scored as medium. Re-verify with rows 1 + 4: row 4 must stop returning exit 5 and must report `passed ≥ 1`.

## QA evidence 2026-11-18 (shift 4, turn 2) — the false green is now proven with counts on both sides

Six `qa_run_tests` measurements this shift (no shell, QA tools only):

| # | call | result |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `suite=pytest:api`, **no paths** | **35 passed, 0 failed (12.3 s) → allow (green)** |
| 2 | `suite=pytest:api`, `paths=["tests"]` | **1431 passed, 3 failed, 1 skipped — 1435 collected (108.6 s) → block/critical** |
| 3 | `suite=pytest`, **no paths** | **1466 passed, 3 failed, 1 skipped — 1470 collected (114.4 s) → block/critical** |
| 4 | `suite=pytest`, `paths=["api/tests/ai/smol"]` | **exit code 4, 0 tests, 1.0 s** → `tests.run-error` |
| 5 | `suite=pytest:api`, `paths=["tests/ai"]` | 150 passed, **1 failed** (151, 14.2 s) → block |
| 6 | `suite=pytest:api`, `paths=["tests/security"]` | 59 passed, 0 failed (11.3 s) → allow |

### What this settles

1. **The green subset is 2.4 % of the tree and contains none of the failures.** `pytest:api` default root = 35 green tests; the real api tree = **1435 tests, 3 failing**. The gate would report `allow` on a red tree — the false green card is confirmed, not suspected.
2. **The default suite cannot be path-scoped at all.** `pytest` (what `qa_review_changes` uses with `suite="auto"`) returns **exit 4 / 0 tests for every `paths=` argument** — probe #4. So on every review the gate executes *zero* tests and reports `tests.run-error`, while 1470 tests exist and 3 of them fail. Both halves of the defect (selection + path form) are real and independent.
3. **The api tree is red today:** 3 failures / 1435. Located so far: 1 in `tests/ai` (same single failure as the earlier record, 14.2 s), `tests/security` clean (59/59), the other 2 in the remaining ~1225 tests.
4. **Attribution is impossible through the gate:** these runs read the working tree, so I cannot say whether the 3 failures come from the staged change or from HEAD — a clean-tree comparison needs a run the gate cannot produce (it never executes). That is a third defect, not a conclusion.

### Acceptance (unchanged + one addition)
- `qa_review_changes(scope="staged")` reports `passed > 0` and the real tree size (≈1435), not 35.
- A path-scoped run of the default suite must not error: `qa_run_tests(suite="pytest", paths=["api/tests/ai/smol"])` must **not** return `exit code 4`.
- Failing runs must carry node-ids (see `d7e0f3fa`).

Next command that re-verifies: `qa_run_tests(suite="pytest", paths=["api/tests/ai/smol"])` → expect tests collected, not exit 4.

## QA 2026-11-18 (shift 4, turn 3) — the false green is confirmed AND a fix recipe for `tests.failed @ -` is proven

Counts on the same tree, same suite:

| run | result |
| --- | --- |
| `qa_run_tests(suite="pytest:api")` (no paths) | **35 passed / 0 failed, 12.3 s → allow** ← the false green |
| `… paths=["tests"]` | **1431 passed / 3 failed / 1 skipped, 1442 collected → block** |
| `… paths=["tests/security"]` | 59 passed, 0 failed → allow |
| `… paths=["tests/ai"]` | 150 passed / 1 failed → block |
| `… paths=["tests/harness"]` | 29 passed / 1 failed → block |

So the declared default root covers **35 of 1442** tests (**2.4 %**), and the real tree is red.

## Fix recipe for the missing node-ids (measured, works today)
`qa_run_tests(..., extra_args=["--junitxml=qa-x.xml"])` writes the report **relative to the suite cwd (`api/`)**, and `project_read_file("api/qa-x.xml")` can read it (an absolute `/tmp/...` path cannot — earlier attempt failed). With a `-k`-narrowed run the report is small enough to show `classname` + `name` verbatim, e.g.:

`testsuite tests="1" failures="1" … <testcase classname="codx-junior-platform.api.tests.harness.test_harness_profile" name="test_workspace_copy_matches_builtin"><failure message="AssertionError: ## What happened missing from …">`

**Acceptance for the gate:** `tests.failed` findings must carry `<classname>::<name>` instead of `@ -`, i.e. the QA runner should always pass `--junitxml` (into a temp path inside the tree) and parse it. That converts today's `tests.failed @ -` into the node-ids a developer can act on — no product change needed.

Two of the three failing node-ids are now posted on card **d7e0f3fa**.

## Side effect to clean up (QA-created, untracked)
My runs left four untracked reports in the tree: `api/qa-shift4.xml`, `api/qa-mt.xml`, `api/qa-harness.xml`, `api/qa-ws.xml`. They must be deleted before any commit (I have no write/shell tool). Suggested permanent fix: make the runner write to a gitignored path (`api/.qa/`) and add that folder to `.gitignore`.
